# ui

Namespace-scope declarations of `ui` from the rendering headers.

## Enumerations

### BevelSides

```cpp
enum class BevelSides : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

Which edges of a bevel draw. Group boxes, status-bar panes and etched separators draw only some of the four. A bit set: combine with `|`.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | No edge. |
| `Left` | The left edge. |
| `Top` | The top edge. |
| `Right` | The right edge. |
| `Bottom` | The bottom edge. |
| `All` | Every edge (the default). |

### Stretch

```cpp
enum class Stretch
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

How content is stretched into its destination rect. The [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) element, [Icon](../controls/icon.md#uiicon), [PersonPicture](../controls/person-picture.md#uipersonpicture), [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer), [ScaleToFit](../layout/scale-to-fit.md#uiscaletofit) and the shapes read it; [fit_stretch()](#fit_stretch) does the math.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | [Native](../controls/native-control.md#uinative) size, centered, cropped by the destination if larger. |
| `Fill` | Distorts to exactly fill the destination on both axes. |
| `Uniform` | Fits inside, aspect kept, one axis letterboxed; the [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) default. |
| `UniformToFill` | Covers the destination, aspect kept, one axis cropped ([PersonPicture](../controls/person-picture.md#uipersonpicture)). |

### ImageOrientation

```cpp
enum class ImageOrientation : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

How a photo's stored pixels have to be turned to be seen upright: the EXIF orientation tag (TIFF tag 274). The values are the tag's own; the names say what the correction is, the way exiftool does. Rotations are clockwise.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Normal` | Already upright. |
| `MirrorHorizontal` | Mirror left-right. |
| `Rotate180` | Rotate 180°. |
| `MirrorVertical` | Mirror top-bottom. |
| `Transpose` | Mirror left-right, then rotate 270°. |
| `Rotate90` | Rotate 90° clockwise (a portrait photo from most phones). |
| `Transverse` | Mirror left-right, then rotate 90°. |
| `Rotate270` | Rotate 270° clockwise. |

### PixelFormat

```cpp
enum class PixelFormat : std::uint8_t
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

How a [Bitmap](bitmap.md)'s bytes are laid out: 4 bytes per pixel, row-major, rows packed with no padding.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Rgba8` | R, G, B, A with straight alpha: the default, and what the decoders and PNG give. |
| `Bgra8Premultiplied` | B, G, R, A with each color already multiplied by alpha: what most rasterizers write, PDFium among them. Drawn as it is, with no conversion on the way. |


Header: `winui/render/Brush.hpp`.

The direction a [LinearGradientBrush](linear-gradient-brush.md) runs across the painted bounds.

### BorderStyle

```cpp
enum class BorderStyle
```

Header: `winui/render/Renderer.hpp`.

How a control's border is drawn: the Fluent fill alone, or a classic 2 px bevel.

Flat and Rounded draw no separate border; the control's fill is the whole look. Raised and Sunken add the Windows 95/98/2000 light/dark bevel around the fill, drawn by [draw_bevel_border()](#draw_bevel_border).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Flat` | Square-cornered fill, no border draw. |
| `Rounded` | Theme-rounded fill, no border draw; the Fluent default. |
| `Raised` | Classic bevel of a control at rest (light top-left, dark bottom-right). |
| `Sunken` | Classic bevel of a pressed or checked control (the colors swapped). |

### Symbol

```cpp
enum class Symbol : char32_t
```

Header: `winui/render/Symbol.hpp`.

Named icons for [ui::Icon](../controls/icon.md#uiicon), [AppBarButton](../controls/app-bar-button.md#uiappbarbutton) and anything else taking an [IconSource](icon-source.md). Each value is the Segoe MDL2 Assets / Segoe Fluent Icons codepoint the symbol draws, so the enumerators need no further description.

A [Symbol](#symbol) converts implicitly to an [IconSource](icon-source.md); [symbol_glyph()](#symbol_glyph) turns one into an [IconGlyph](icon-glyph.md).

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::CommandBar{
    .primary = {ui::AppBarButton{.text = "Save", .icon = ui::Symbol::Save},
                ui::AppBarButton{.text = "Share", .icon = ui::Symbol::Share}},
});

const ui::Rect search_rect{8.0f, 8.0f, 16.0f, 16.0f};
ui::draw_icon(renderer, ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Find, 16.0f), search_rect, theme.palette.text_fill_primary);
```

### TextAlign

```cpp
enum class TextAlign
```

Header: `winui/render/Text.hpp`.

Where a text run sits inside the box it is drawn into, per axis ([TextStyle::horizontal](text-style.md#horizontal) and [TextStyle::vertical](text-style.md#vertical)). Leading/Trailing are left/right horizontally and top/bottom vertically.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Leading` | Left edge horizontally, top edge vertically. |
| `Center` | Centered on the axis ([TextStyle](text-style.md)'s default for both axes). |
| `Trailing` | Right edge horizontally, bottom edge vertically. |

### TextRole

```cpp
enum class TextRole
```

Header: `winui/render/Text.hpp`.

The semantic role a run of text plays on a page: what [`TextControl::set_role()`](../controls/text.md#set_role) (and [`ui::Text::role`](../controls/text.md#uitext-role)) takes and [`Theme::TypeRamp::for_role()`](../themes/theme.md#for_role) resolves against the active theme's fonts. `Body` is the default, so a plain, role-less [`TextControl`](../controls/text.md#uitextcontrol) reads as body text.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::Text{.text = "Settings", .role = ui::TextRole::Title},
        ui::Text{.text = "Changes apply immediately.", .role = ui::TextRole::Caption},
    },
});
```

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Body` | Running body text; the default. |
| `Header` | Largest display rung (a page or hub header). |
| `Subheader` | [Section](../controls/sections.md#uisection) header one rung below Header. |
| `Title` | Page or dialog title. |
| `Subtitle` | Group heading below a Title. |
| `Caption` | Small secondary text (hints, timestamps). |
| `BodyStrong` | Body text at the ramp's SemiBold, for a label that heads the content below it. An era that sets no rung of its own gets its body style in SemiBold. |

### TextEffectKind

```cpp
enum class TextEffectKind
```

Header: `winui/render/Text.hpp`.

Which extra rendering pass a [TextEffect](text-effect.md) applies. The classic disabled label is `Emboss`: the string is drawn twice, once in the highlight color offset by (1,1) and then in the shadow color at the origin, for an engraved look. `None` (the default) keeps a single plain pass.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | One plain pass in the run's own color. |
| `Emboss` | Highlight pass at the offset, then the shadow pass on the origin. |

### TextWrapping

```cpp
enum class TextWrapping
```

Header: `winui/render/Text.hpp`.

Whether a run breaks onto further lines when it meets the width it is laid out in. `Wrap` breaks between words, and inside a word too long for a line on its own. `WrapWholeWords` never splits a word and lets one that doesn't fit overflow instead. Explicit line breaks (`\n`) start a new line in either mode.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `NoWrap` | Everything on one line; the default. |
| `Wrap` | Break between words, and inside a word too long for a line. |
| `WrapWholeWords` | Break only between words; an overlong word overflows. |

### draw_bevel_border

```cpp
void draw_bevel_border(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, BorderStyle style, const Color& light, const Color& highlight, const Color& shadow, const Color& dark_shadow, float step, BevelSides sides = BevelSides::All, bool soft = false, int rings = 2)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

Draws a classic 3D border around `bounds`, two concentric rings of `step` width: Raised (a control at rest): the top and left get `light` outside `highlight`, the bottom and right get `dark_shadow` outside `shadow`. Sunken (a pressed or checked control): the same shape mirrored. The top and left get `shadow` outside `dark_shadow`, the bottom and right get `highlight` outside `light`. `step` is usually [Theme::border_width](../themes/theme.md#border_width), 1 DIP in every classic theme. `sides` picks which of the four edges draw (default: all). Any other [BorderStyle](#borderstyle) draws nothing.

`soft` is the arrangement a push button is drawn with. It swaps the two top and left rings and leaves the bottom and right alone, so a soft raised button has `highlight` outside `light` on its lit side, where a window border has `light` outside `highlight`.

The outer ring runs the full length of each edge. The inner ring stops one step short at each corner where both adjoining edges draw, so the two rings nest without overlapping.

`rings` is how many of the two rings to draw. Every framed surface draws two. One draws the outer ring alone, the shape of a hot toolbar button. That shape takes the inner color pair on its one ring, so its caller passes `light == highlight` and `dark_shadow == shadow`. `highlight` and `shadow` go unread at `rings == 1`.

Every edge is a [Renderer::stroke_line()](renderer.md#stroke_line): eight [StrokeLine](render-commands.md#struct-strokeline) commands for a two-ring border on all four sides.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Color light       = ui::Color::from_rgba(223, 223, 223);
const ui::Color highlight   = ui::colors::White;
const ui::Color shadow      = ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 128, 128);
const ui::Color dark_shadow = ui::colors::Black;
const ui::Rect  bounds{0, 0, 75, 23};
const ui::Rect  pane{0, 0, 120, 20};

// A Windows 95 push button at rest, and the same button pressed.
ui::draw_bevel_border(renderer, bounds, ui::BorderStyle::Raised, light, highlight, shadow,
                         dark_shadow, 1.0f, ui::BevelSides::All, /*soft=*/true);
ui::draw_bevel_border(renderer, bounds, ui::BorderStyle::Sunken, light, highlight, shadow,
                         dark_shadow, 1.0f);

// A status-bar pane separator: the left and right edges only.
ui::draw_bevel_border(renderer, pane, ui::BorderStyle::Sunken, light, highlight, shadow,
                         dark_shadow, 1.0f, ui::BevelSides::Left | ui::BevelSides::Right);
```

### draw_win3x_border

```cpp
void draw_win3x_border(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, BorderStyle style, const Color& frame, const Color& highlight, const Color& shadow, float step, float radius = 0.0f)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

Draws the Windows 3.x border around `bounds`, which is lopsided where [draw_bevel_border()](#draw_bevel_border) is symmetric:

raised: 1px `frame` on all four sides (outermost) 1px `highlight` on the top and left, inside it 2px `shadow` on the right and bottom, inside it pressed: 1px `frame` on all four sides 1px `shadow` on the top and left, and no bottom or right edge

Content inside this border sits off center, 2px in from the top and left and 3px from the right and bottom, which suits the era's pressed content offset of one pixel right and down.

`radius` rounds the frame only, for the push button, the era's one round-cornered surface. The highlight and shadow inside the frame stay straight. Pass 0 for every other surface. `step` is the width of the 1px units above, in DIPs. Flat and Rounded styles draw nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Color frame     = ui::colors::Black;
const ui::Color highlight = ui::colors::White;
const ui::Color shadow    = ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 128, 128);
const ui::Rect  bounds{0, 0, 75, 23};
const bool      pressed = false;

// A Windows 3.1 push button: rounded frame, raised at rest, pressed while held.
const ui::BorderStyle style = pressed ? ui::BorderStyle::Sunken : ui::BorderStyle::Raised;
ui::draw_win3x_border(renderer, bounds, style, frame, highlight, shadow, 1.0f, /*radius=*/2.0f);
```

### draw_classic_radio

```cpp
void draw_classic_radio(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& box, const Color& light, const Color& highlight, const Color& shadow, const Color& dark_shadow, const Color& well, const std::optional<Color>& dot)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

The classic radio button, drawn per device pixel at the target's own scale ([Renderer::device_scale()](renderer.md#device_scale)): the sunken bevel made round, two one-pixel rings split along the diagonal from the top-right to the bottom-left corner, around a `well` disc.

outer ring: `shadow` on the top/left half, `highlight` on the bottom/right inner ring: `dark_shadow` on the top/left half, `light` on the bottom/right dot: `dot`, a disc a little under half the ring's width, when set

At 96 DPI the ring is 12 x 12 inside a 13 x 13 `box`, with the spare column on the left and the spare row at the bottom, and the dot is 4 x 4 with its corners cut, matching the classic radio button pixel for pixel. Larger scales draw the same shape at their own size (a 14 px ring at 125 %, 18 at 150 %, 20 at 175 %) instead of scaling the 12 px one. Each ring stays one device pixel wide up to 200 %, where it becomes two.

Example: 
```cpp
// A checked Windows 95 radio button.
ui::draw_classic_radio(renderer, ui::Rect{0, 0, 13, 13},
                       ui::Color::from_rgba(223, 223, 223), ui::colors::White,
                       ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 128, 128), ui::colors::Black,
                       ui::colors::White, ui::colors::Black);
```

### draw_classic_arrow

```cpp
void draw_classic_arrow(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& area, ArrowDirection direction, const Color& color, float depth = 4.0f)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

The classic solid arrow: a 45-degree triangle `depth` DIPs deep with a base of `2 * depth - 1`, centered in `area` and drawn per device pixel ([Renderer::device_scale()](renderer.md#device_scale)), so its sides stay true diagonals at any scale. The default depth 4 is the 7 x 4 arrow every classic scroll bar, spin button, combo box and drop-down carries at 96 DPI.

Example: 
```cpp
// A combo box's drop button arrow, and a menu item's cascade arrow.
const ui::Rect button_rect{104, 2, 16, 17};
const ui::Rect cascade_rect{140, 0, 16, 18};
ui::draw_classic_arrow(renderer, button_rect, ui::ArrowDirection::Down, ui::colors::Black);
ui::draw_classic_arrow(renderer, cascade_rect, ui::ArrowDirection::Right, ui::colors::Black);
```

### draw_classic_tree_button

```cpp
void draw_classic_tree_button(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& area, bool expanded, const Color& frame, const Color& well, const Color& sign)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bevel.hpp`.

The classic tree view's expand button: a 9 x 9 box in a one-pixel `frame` around a `well`, holding a 5 px plus while collapsed or a minus while expanded, in `sign`. Centered in `area` and drawn per device pixel like [draw_classic_arrow()](#draw_classic_arrow).

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Rect chevron_rect{0, 0, 16, 16};
const bool     node_expanded = true;
ui::draw_classic_tree_button(renderer, chevron_rect, node_expanded,
                             ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 128, 128), ui::colors::White, ui::colors::Black);
```

```cpp
bool swaps_axes(ImageOrientation orientation)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

Whether `orientation` swaps width and height.

### compare

```cpp
ImageDiff compare(const Bitmap& a, const Bitmap& b, int threshold = 0)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

Compares two images. A pixel mismatches when any channel differs by more than `threshold`. Two images in different formats are compared as RGBA.

### fit_stretch

```cpp
Rect fit_stretch(const Rect& bounds, Size natural, Stretch stretch)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

Fits a `natural` (unstretched) size into `bounds` per `stretch`, returning the resulting centered destination rect. [Renderer::draw_image()](renderer.md#draw_image) fits an image's pixel size the same way, and [AnimatedVisualPlayer](../controls/animated-visual-player.md#uianimatedvisualplayer) and [AnimatedIcon](../controls/animated-icon.md#uianimatedicon) use this to fit caller-drawn content. With UniformToFill and None the result may extend past `bounds`, so clip if that matters. A zero-area `natural` size returns `bounds` unchanged.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Rect dest = ui::fit_stretch(ui::Rect{0, 0, 200, 100}, ui::Size{50, 50},
                                            ui::Stretch::Uniform);
// dest == {50, 0, 100, 100}: scaled to the height and centered horizontally.
```

### fit_within

```cpp
std::pair<int, int> fit_within(int width, int height, int max_width, int max_height)
```

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

The size `width` × `height` shrinks to inside `max_width` × `max_height` (zero: unconstrained), aspect ratio kept, rounded to whole pixels and never below 1. Never larger than the input. What [Bitmap::scaled_to_fit()](bitmap.md#scaled_to_fit) and the decoders size their output by.

### stroke_rounded_rect_inside

```cpp
void stroke_rounded_rect_inside(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float corner_radius, const Color& color, float width)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

Strokes a control's border so the whole ring lands inside `bounds`.

A stroke covers half its width on each side of its path, so a border centered on a control's rect puts half of itself outside it. A clipping parent, such as [`SwipeControl`](../layout/swipe.md#uiswipecontrol), cuts that outer half on all four sides, and under an aliased, pixel-snapped theme the remaining half pixel rounds away. A border drawn inside never extends past its layout slot, like the edges of [draw_bevel_border()](#draw_bevel_border) and [draw_win3x_border()](#draw_win3x_border).

The path moves in by half a stroke, and the radius with it, so the ring's outer edge stays on the rect and corner the caller asked for. `width` is in DIPs.

Example: 
```cpp
// A 2px outline whose outer edge sits exactly on bounds, corner radius 4.
const ui::Rect bounds{0, 0, 120, 32};
ui::stroke_rounded_rect_inside(renderer, bounds, 4.0f, theme.colors().text, 2.0f);
```

### stroke_rounded_rect_gradient_inside

```cpp
void stroke_rounded_rect_gradient_inside(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float corner_radius, const LinearGradientBrush& brush, float extent_px, float width)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

The gradient counterpart of [stroke_rounded_rect_inside()](#stroke_rounded_rect_inside), for Fluent's elevation border. `extent_px` keeps its meaning, because the renderer anchors it at the edge of the path it strokes, which moves in with it. See [StrokeRoundedRectGradient](render-commands.md#struct-strokeroundedrectgradient) for its sign.

### draw_control_chrome

```cpp
void draw_control_chrome(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float corner_radius, const ButtonVisual& visual, float border_width, bool draw_flat_border_fallback = false, bool use_border_gradient = true)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

Draws `visual`'s background fill and border around `bounds` at `corner_radius`, in this order:
1. The background: `visual.background_gradient` if set (XP and Vista chrome), else a flat `visual.background` fill.
1. `visual.inner_shadow` if set (Aero's pressed state): two 2px bands fading out from the top and left edges, over the fill and under the border. No other theme sets it.
1. `visual.inset_well` if set (Aero's check box): a square rim and a square fill inside the well, both diagonal gradients, under the border.
1. The border, at most one of: a. A bevel when `visual.border_style` is Raised or Sunken (the 3.x through 2000 chrome): [draw_win3x_border()](#draw_win3x_border) when the visual has a `bevel_frame`, else [draw_bevel_border()](#draw_bevel_border). Nothing is drawn after a bevel. b. Otherwise `visual.border_gradient`, if set and `use_border_gradient` is true: Fluent's elevation border on a button at rest or under the pointer. A check box's checked visual carries one too, and the check box passes `use_border_gradient = false` to leave it undrawn. c. Otherwise a flat stroke of `visual.border`, when `draw_flat_border_fallback` or `visual.draw_border` is true. Buttons pass false, so their pressed, disabled and subtle states stay borderless, and a button visual that wants an outline sets [`draw_border`](#draw_border) itself, as Metro's dark button does. A check box passes true, so its box always shows an outline when there's no bevel. b and c are stroked inside `bounds` (see [stroke_rounded_rect_inside()](#stroke_rounded_rect_inside)).
1. `visual.inner_border` if set (Aero, Luna): an `inner_border_width` gradient ring stroked inside the rect the border leaves, at the radius less the border. It is the innermost layer, so it comes last.

Every border is drawn at `visual.resolved_border_width()`: a visual's own [`ButtonVisual::border_width`](../themes/button-visual.md#border_width) overrides the theme-wide `border_width` passed here, so one theme can give a button a 2px outline and a check box none at the same time.

[Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) and content are the caller's to draw afterwards; the window draws the focus ring.

Example: 
```cpp
class MyButton : public ui::Element
{
    bool        pressed_ = false;
    std::string label_   = "OK";

    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme&        theme = context.theme;
        const ui::ButtonVisual& v     = pressed_ ? theme.button_pressed : theme.button_normal;
        ui::draw_control_chrome(renderer, bounds(), theme.resolved_button_corner_radius(), v,
                                theme.border_width);
        renderer.draw_text(label_, bounds(), v.text, ui::TextStyle{});
    }
};
```

### draw_disclosure

```cpp
void draw_disclosure(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, const IconGlyph& glyph, ArrowDirection classic, const Rect& area, const Color& color, float glyph_size = 0.0f)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

An expand, collapse or drop-down mark in `area`: the icon font's `glyph` at `glyph_size` (0 for the glyph's own size) in `theme.icon_font_family`, or, under a theme whose `disclosure_visual` is ThemeDisclosureVisual::ClassicArrow, the era's solid 7 x 4 arrow pointing `classic` ([draw_classic_arrow()](#draw_classic_arrow)). Every control with such a mark draws it through this call, so a theme changes all of them at once.

Example: 
```cpp
// An Expander's header mark: a chevron, or a solid arrow in the classic packs.
const bool     expanded = true;
const ui::Rect chevron_rect{200, 8, 16, 16};
ui::draw_disclosure(renderer, theme, expanded ? ui::glyphs::ChevronUp : ui::glyphs::ChevronDown,
                    expanded ? ui::ArrowDirection::Up : ui::ArrowDirection::Down, chevron_rect,
                    theme.colors().text, 12.0f);
```

### fill_overlay_surface

```cpp
void fill_overlay_surface(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, const Rect& bounds, float corner_radius, const Color& fallback)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

A popup's surface: `theme.overlay_material` (in-app acrylic) when the theme has one, drawn through [Renderer::draw_geometry()](renderer.md#draw_geometry) with `fallback` as the color a renderer that cannot blur paints, and a plain `fallback` fill otherwise. `fallback` is the surface's solid color, usually `theme.surfaces.menu`. Acrylic blurs what was drawn before it, so fill the surface first, then draw its content.

Example: 
```cpp
// A custom flyout's background.
const ui::Rect bounds{0, 0, 240, 160};
ui::fill_overlay_surface(renderer, theme, bounds, theme.overlay_corner_radius, theme.surfaces.menu);
```

### draw_border

```cpp
void draw_border(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, const std::optional<Color>& background, const std::optional<Color>& border_brush, const Thickness& thickness, float corner_radius)
```

Header: `winui/render/Chrome.hpp`.

A bordered box's background and border, as a [Border](../layout/border.md#uiborder) or a panel draws them: the background fills the rect inside the border, at the corner radius less the border, and the border is laid inside `bounds`. Either color may be absent, which draws nothing for that layer.

A uniform `thickness` strokes one rounded ring. A non-uniform one fills the four edges as straight bands, so a rounded corner between two different widths comes out square.

Example: 
```cpp
// What ui::BorderControl::render_override() does with its own properties.
const ui::Rect bounds{0, 0, 200, 120};
ui::draw_border(renderer, bounds, ui::Color::from_rgba(243, 243, 243),
                   ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 0, 0, 40), ui::Thickness{1}, 8.0f);
```

### describe

```cpp
std::string describe(const std::vector<RenderCommand>& commands)
```

Header: `winui/render/Describe.hpp`.

A stable text dump of a render-command stream: one line per command, fields in a fixed order, floats at two decimals, colors as `#RRGGBBAA`. Golden-file tests compare against it, since it doesn't depend on resolution, fonts or the operating system.

[Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) and SVG commands print their sizes, not their contents. [ui::testing::describe()](../testing/namespace-ui-testing.md#describe) prints a whole window.

Example: 
```cpp
// A renderer of your own, an export backend say, can keep each call as a RenderCommand
// and log a frame in this format.
class ExportRenderer : public ui::Renderer
{
public:
    void fill_rounded_rect(const ui::Rect& bounds, float radius, const ui::Color& color) override
    {
        frame_.push_back(ui::FillRoundedRect{bounds, radius, color});
        // ... draw it ...
    }

    // After an element has rendered into it:
    void log_frame() const
    {
        std::println("{}", ui::describe(frame_));
        //   FillRoundedRect rect=(0.00,0.00,10.00,10.00) radius=2.00 color=`#FFFFFFFF`
    }

private:
    std::vector<ui::RenderCommand> frame_;
};
```

### draw_dotted_rect

```cpp
void draw_dotted_rect(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, const Color& color, float dash_length = 1.0f, float phase = 0.0f)
```

Header: `winui/render/FocusRing.hpp`.

Draws a 1px dotted rectangle around `bounds`. The caller insets `bounds` from the control's edges first, leaving a few pixels between the bevel or fill and the dots. Dots are `dash_length`-long strokes of `color` separated by an equal gap, starting `phase` into the first gap. The default, 1px dashes at phase 0, alternates every pixel like the classic focus rect. Metro's dashed pair ([draw_focus_ring()](#draw_focus_ring)) draws this twice, one dash apart, so one color's dashes land exactly in the other's gaps. Each dash is a [Renderer::stroke_line()](renderer.md#stroke_line).

Example: 
```cpp
// The classic focus rect, 4px inside a Windows 95 button.
const ui::Rect bounds{0, 0, 75, 23};
ui::draw_dotted_rect(renderer, bounds.inset(ui::Thickness{4}), ui::colors::Black);
```

### draw_focus_ring_at

```cpp
void draw_focus_ring_at(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, const Thickness& outward, float radius, const FocusRingStyle& style)
```

Header: `winui/render/FocusRing.hpp`.

Draws a focus visual at its own distance from each side of `bounds`. For the Fluent rings, the outer ring's outer edge lands `outward` outside `bounds` on each side, inside for a negative side. [`FocusRingStyle::margin`](focus-ring-style.md#margin), 3 on every side, is the usual distance, and the few controls that differ pass their own. Any other kind of focus visual is drawn around `bounds`, as [draw_focus_ring()](#draw_focus_ring) draws it.

Example: 
```cpp
// A check box rings box and label as one unit, 7 out at the sides and 3 above and below.
const ui::FocusRingStyle style = theme.focus_ring_style();
const ui::Rect           content_rect{0, 0, 120, 20};
ui::draw_focus_ring_at(renderer, content_rect, ui::Symmetric{.horizontal = 7.0f, .vertical = 3.0f}, 4.0f, style);
```

### draw_focus_ring_rings

```cpp
void draw_focus_ring_rings(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius, const FocusRingStyle& style)
```

Header: `winui/render/FocusRing.hpp`.

Draws the Fluent two-ring focus visual, whatever `style.kind` says: a `style.outer_width` ring in `style.outer_color` whose outer edge lands `style.margin` outside `bounds`, and a `style.inner_width` ring in `style.inner_color` touching it on the inside. Both follow the control's corner `radius`, adjusted for each ring's distance, so the band stays concentric with the control's rounding. Use it instead of [draw_focus_ring()](#draw_focus_ring) in a control whose classic dotted rect needs other bounds than its rings, such as [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox).

Example: 
```cpp
// CheckBox: the modern ring hugs the box, while the classic dotted rect wraps the label.
const ui::FocusRingStyle style = theme.focus_ring_style();
const ui::Rect           box_rect{0, 0, 20, 20};
const ui::Rect           label_rect{28, 0, 80, 20};
if (style.kind == ui::FocusVisual::FluentRings)
{
    ui::draw_focus_ring_rings(renderer, box_rect, 4.0f, style);
}
else
{
    ui::draw_focus_ring(renderer, label_rect, 0.0f, style);
}
```

### draw_focus_ring

```cpp
void draw_focus_ring(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius, const FocusRingStyle& style)
```

Header: `winui/render/FocusRing.hpp`.

Draws the focus visual `style.kind` calls for around `bounds`, at the control's corner `radius`: ClassicDotted: a dotted rect inset 4px ([draw_dotted_rect()](#draw_dotted_rect)). MetroDashedPair: the same inset rect drawn twice, `outer_color` at phase 0 and `inner_color` at phase `style.dash_length`, so one color's dashes fill the other's gaps. FluentRings: [draw_focus_ring_rings()](#draw_focus_ring_rings). Every focusable control except [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox) uses the same `bounds` for all three, so this is the one call most render_override() implementations need.

Example: 
```cpp
class MyControl : public ui::Element
{
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        // ... the control's own drawing ...
        if (is_focused() && focus_visible())
        {
            const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
            ui::draw_focus_ring(renderer, bounds(), theme.corner_radius, theme.focus_ring_style());
        }
    }
};
```

### draw_icon

```cpp
void draw_icon(Renderer& renderer, const IconGlyph& glyph, const Rect& bounds, const Color& color, float size_override = 0.0f, std::string_view font_family = {})
```

Header: `winui/render/IconGlyph.hpp`.

Draws `glyph` centered in `bounds` through [Renderer::draw_text()](renderer.md#draw_text), in `color` at `size_override` (or `glyph.size` when `size_override` is 0, the default).

`font_family`, when not empty, overrides the glyph's own family. A theme picks its era's symbol font this way through [`Theme::icon_font_family`](../themes/theme.md#icon_font_family): `Segoe MDL2 Assets` or `Segoe Fluent Icons`, which draw the same codepoints in two styles.

Example: 
```cpp
// InfoBar's icon: a filled circle, then the symbol on top, both at 16.
const ui::Rect  icon_rect{12, 14, 16, 16};
const ui::Color severity_color = ui::Color::from_rgba(196, 43, 28);
ui::draw_icon(renderer, ui::glyphs::CircleFill, icon_rect, severity_color, 16.0f, theme.icon_font_family);
ui::draw_icon(renderer, ui::glyphs::Important, icon_rect, ui::colors::White, 16.0f, theme.icon_font_family);
```

### draw_drop_shadow

```cpp
void draw_drop_shadow(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius, const ShadowRecipe& recipe)
```

Header: `winui/render/OverlayShadow.hpp`.

Draws `recipe`'s two shadows behind a surface occupying `bounds` (a rounded rect at `radius`). Call before drawing the surface's own background so its fill paints over the shadow's center.

[Renderer](renderer.md) has no blur, so each shadow is a stack of up to eight nested fill_rounded_rect() calls whose alphas composite to a Gaussian edge. The shadow reaches up to one blur radius past `bounds`, so leave room there or don't clip it. A recipe that doesn't cast draws nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Rect bounds{16, 16, 200, 32};
ui::draw_drop_shadow(renderer, bounds, theme.overlay_corner_radius,
                     ui::ShadowRecipe::for_elevation(ui::elevation_z::ToolTip, theme.dark));
```

### draw_aero_popup_shadow

```cpp
void draw_aero_popup_shadow(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius)
```

Header: `winui/render/OverlayShadow.hpp`.

Aero's popup drop shadow, separate from the Fluent recipe above. Aero has no elevation scale and casts no shadow under a button, card or panel. It casts this one only, under a menu, submenu, tooltip, combo box drop-down or toolbar overflow.

The shape: the popup's own rect moved 5 px right and down and filled `#71000000`. The whole shadow lies inside that rect: a solid center 5 px in from each side, wrapped in a 5 px fall-off band, with round corners at `radius + 5`. Because the rect moves by exactly the band width, the top and left bands land under the popup, and a user sees a 5 px shadow down the right and along the bottom. A caller reserves a 5 px strip on the right and bottom of the popup for it.

Example: 
```cpp
// Under a Vista menu popup, before its own background and border.
const ui::Rect popup_bounds{0, 0, 180, 120};
ui::draw_aero_popup_shadow(renderer, popup_bounds, 0.0f);
renderer.fill_rounded_rect(popup_bounds, 0.0f, theme.surfaces.menu);
```

### draw_overlay_shadow

```cpp
void draw_overlay_shadow(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius, bool dark, float z = elevation_z::Flyout)
```

Header: `winui/render/OverlayShadow.hpp`.

Draws a popup's drop shadow. A light-dismiss surface ([Flyout](../controls/flyout.md#uiflyout), [MenuFlyout](../controls/menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout), the [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox) popup) sits at elevation 32, the default `z`. A tooltip is the one popup that sits a step lower, at [`elevation_z::ToolTip`](namespace-ui-elevation_z.md#tooltip). `dark` picks the dark-theme alphas; pass `theme.dark`.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Rect flyout_bounds{0, 0, 240, 160};
ui::draw_overlay_shadow(renderer, flyout_bounds, theme.overlay_corner_radius, theme.dark);
renderer.fill_rounded_rect(flyout_bounds, theme.overlay_corner_radius, theme.surfaces.menu);
```

### word_run

